requirements.title: DSHIFTL argument restrictions
requirements.definition: I and J shall be integer or BOZ literal constants with matching integer kinds when both are integer, shall not both be BOZ literals, and SHIFT shall be an integer in the permitted nonnegative BIT_SIZE range for DSHIFTL.

pending.DSHIFTL-I-integer-or-boz: Positive plan calls DSHIFTL with integer I and BOZ-literal I variants; source-control mutation changes I to real and claims no diagnostic facet.
pending.DSHIFTL-J-integer-or-boz: Positive plan calls DSHIFTL with integer J and BOZ-literal J variants; source-control mutation changes J to real and claims no diagnostic facet.
pending.DSHIFTL-integer-kinds-match: Positive plan uses same-kind integer I and J; source-control mutation uses different integer kinds and claims no diagnostic facet.
pending.DSHIFTL-not-both-boz: Positive plan uses exactly one BOZ literal with one integer operand; source-control mutation makes both operands BOZ literals and claims no diagnostic facet.
pending.DSHIFTL-SHIFT-integer-nonnegative-in-ran: Positive plan uses SHIFT values 0, 1, and BIT_SIZE(I); source-control mutations use -1 and BIT_SIZE(I)+1 and claim no diagnostic facet.

requirements.title: DSHIFTL result characteristics follow the integer operand
requirements.definition: The result of DSHIFTL has the same type and kind as I when I is integer, otherwise the same type and kind as J.

requirements.title: DSHIFTL converts a BOZ operand as INT to the other integer kind
requirements.definition: If either I or J is a BOZ literal constant, DSHIFTL first converts it as if by INT to integer with the kind type parameter of the other operand.

pending.DSHIFTL-boz-converted-as-int-to-other-ki: Use exact-one-BOZ calls DSHIFTL(Z'03', J_int, 2) and DSHIFTL(I_int, Z'03', BIT_SIZE(I_int)-1), where J_int has only bits BIT_SIZE(J_int)-1 and 0 set and I_int has only bit 0 set. Observe the result only with BTEST: the first call sets bits 1, 2, and 3; the second sets bits 0 and BIT_SIZE(I_int)-1. Compare with companion calls that explicitly convert the BOZ literal with INT to the other operand's kind, and mutate the BOZ literal to Z'01' to clear a predicted bit.

requirements.title: DSHIFTL result bit composition and intrinsic equivalence
requirements.definition: The DSHIFTL result is formed from shifted bits of I and J and is equal to IOR(SHIFTL(I,SHIFT), SHIFTR(J,BIT_SIZE(J)-SHIFT)); the integer-as-bits model is the one in 16.3.

pending.DSHIFTL-shifted-bits-from-operands: Use I with only bits 0 and 2 set, J with only bits BIT_SIZE(J)-1 and BIT_SIZE(J)-3 set, and SHIFT=4. Assert by BTEST, not numeric value, that the result has exactly bits 1, 3, 4, and 6 set among the observed positions; mutating argument order or SHIFT changes those bit positions.
pending.DSHIFTL-ior-shift-equivalence: For the same discriminating I, J, and SHIFT=4, compute RESULT=DSHIFTL(I,J,SHIFT) and EXPECT=IOR(SHIFTL(I,SHIFT), SHIFTR(J,BIT_SIZE(J)-SHIFT)); compare the bit patterns by BTEST over positions 0 through 7 and the two source high-bit positions, never by interpreting the numeric value.
pending.DSHIFTL-shift-zero-and-full-width-edges: Use I with only bits 0 and BIT_SIZE(I)-2 set and J with only bits 1 and BIT_SIZE(J)-1 set. Assert by BTEST that DSHIFTL(I,J,0) has I's selected bit pattern and not J's selected-only bit, and that DSHIFTL(I,J,BIT_SIZE(I)) has J's selected bit pattern and not I's selected-only bit.
